title: The Mirror's Shadow
summary: Leo buys a mysterious old mirror for his room suddenly.

sentences.text: Leo had recently moved into a large, quiet house that was situated near the edge of an old, historic town.
He wanted to find some unique furniture, so he visited a small shop where various beautiful things were sold cheap.
A large mirror with a dark wooden frame immediately caught his eye because it looked extremely ancient and special.
If he had known about the mirror's strange history, he probably would have chosen a different object for his bedroom.
However, he bought it without delay and hung it on the wall directly opposite his comfortable new bed.
That first evening, the glass reflected his room perfectly, showing nothing but the clean floor and his own happy face.
During the first night, Leo woke up suddenly because the air in his bedroom had become surprisingly cold and thin.
He sat up in bed, opened his eyes, and looked at the large mirror which was shining under the moon.
In the reflection, he noticed a dark shadow sitting quietly on a wooden chair that was placed near the window.
However, when he turned his head to look at the actual room, he realized that no such chair existed there.
The shadow in the mirror did not move, but its presence made him feel an intense sense of deep worry.
He tried to convince himself that it was merely a strange effect caused by the trees outside his window.
On the second night, Leo watched the mirror carefully before he decided to turn off the light near his bed.
When he woke up during the night, he immediately looked at the glass to see if the figure was still there.
The shadow was indeed there, but it was no longer sitting on the silent chair near the far wall.
Instead, the dark figure was now standing, having taken one clear step forward toward the center of the reflected room.
If the shadow had been a real person, Leo would have heard the sound of steps on the wooden floor.
But the bedroom remained completely silent, which only made the growing situation seem much more frightening and real to him.
By the third night, the shadow had taken another step, moving closer to the bed where Leo lay awake.
He decided that he must remove the mirror from his bedroom, believing that this action would solve his terrible problem.
He tried to pull the heavy frame off the wall, but it was held by some strange, unknown force.
No matter how hard he pulled, the mirror would not move, as if it had become part of the house.
He felt a sudden panic rising in his chest, realizing that he was completely unable to escape this bad dream.
He covered the glass with a thick white sheet, hoping that he would not have to look at it again.
However, when he woke up during the fourth night, the sheet was lying on the floor, completely dry and clean.
It was as if some hands had gently removed the cover while he was sleeping deeply in his bed.
He looked into the mirror and saw that the shadow had taken two more steps, standing right in the middle.
The figure, which was dark and had no clear face, was now staring directly at him through the glass.
Leo wanted to run out of the house, but his legs felt extremely heavy, as if they were made of stone.
He could only lie there, watching the shadow that seemed to grow larger and more dangerous with every passing minute.
The next morning, Leo visited the local library to find some information about the old house and its previous owners.
He read through several old books and records, hoping to discover the origin of the terrible mirror he had bought.
He discovered that a young man had once lived in his bedroom many decades ago, before disappearing without a trace.
According to the reports, the young man had spent his last days staring into the same large, dark mirror.
If the young man had destroyed the mirror, he would probably have survived his terrible experience and remained alive.
This discovery filled Leo with a deep fear, as he realized that the same thing was currently happening to him.
When the fifth night arrived, Leo decided to stay awake, keeping all the lights in his bedroom turned on.
However, late at night, every single light in the house suddenly went out, leaving his room in complete and heavy darkness.
In the mirror, which seemed to have its own cold light, the shadow was standing at the very edge.
It was so close that it seemed ready to step out of the glass and enter his real room.
Leo could hear a quiet, cold whisper that seemed to come directly from the other side of the glass.
The whisper was calling his name, over and over, with a voice that was both quiet and extremely ancient.
On the sixth night, Leo knew that he had run out of time and could no longer avoid the shadow.
The dark figure in the mirror had finally reached the absolute front, its hands pressed against the glass surface.
Suddenly, the glass did not look solid anymore; instead, it began to move like water under a gentle wind.
A cold, dark hand slowly emerged from the mirror, reaching out toward Leo who was frozen with extreme fear.
If he had run away on the first day, he would have been safe from this terrible house.
But now, the cold fingers touched his skin, and he felt himself being pulled slowly into the dark reflection.
The next day, the house was completely empty, and the local police could find no trace of the young man.
His bed was completely empty, and the beautiful mirror was still hanging on the wall, shining in the morning light.
A few weeks later, all of Leo's furniture was sold to a local shop that dealt in old, interesting items.
Another customer, who had just moved into a new apartment nearby, bought the large mirror with the wooden frame.
If she knew what was waiting inside the glass, she would certainly have left the mirror in the shop.
But she smiled, took it home, and hung it in her bedroom, where a dark shadow was already waiting.

Leo successfully broke the mirror with a heavy object.
A cold hand emerged from the mirror and pulled Leo inside.

sentences.text: Leo had recently taken possession of a sprawling, silent house that perched on the fringe of an ancient, cobblestone town.
The rooms were bathed in pale morning light, their high ceilings echoing the faint creak of settling timber.
Seeking a piece of character for his new bedroom, Leo wandered into a cramped antique shop where dust seemed to settle like a veil.
Among the assorted bric-a-brac, a tall mirror framed in dark, gnawed wood seized his attention, its surface blackened by age and mystery.
He bought it without hesitation, unaware that the object's hidden past would soon eclipse the comfort of his freshly made bed.
Back at the house, he fixed the mirror to the wall directly opposite his newly arranged bed, the frame fitting the stone as if it had always belonged there.
That night, the moonlit light slipped through the narrow window, casting a silver sheen across the glass that reflected his tidy room with uncanny precision.
He smiled at his own relaxed expression, feeling a fleeting sense of triumph at having found such a unique ornament for his sanctuary.
The house settled around him, the old floorboards sighing in rhythm with his breathing, and a gentle chill brushed his skin as sleep claimed him.
Unaware of the darkness gathering behind the glass, Leo drifted into dreams, his thoughts unburdened by the unseen presence that would soon awaken.
At the stroke of midnight a sudden cold seeped into the bedroom, thin as a whisper, jolting Leo from slumber.
He sat up, heart hammering, and the moon-lit mirror glimmered with an eerie glow that seemed to pulse with a life of its own.
In the reflection, a dark silhouette perched silently upon a wooden chair placed near the window, its outline stark against the pale floor.
When he turned his head to scan the actual room, his eyes fell on empty space; no chair stood there, only the bare wall.
A wave of unease surged through him, yet he tried to rationalize the image as a trick of moonlight and trembling trees.
The following evening, Leo kept the bedroom lamp dim, his eyes trained on the glass as he prepared to sleep.
When the darkness pressed against his eyelids, he glanced at the mirror, half-expecting the phantom chair to have vanished.
The shadow was still there, but now it stood, having taken a single, deliberate step toward the centre of the reflected room.
If a living being had occupied the space, the floor would have announced its presence with a soft creak, yet the silence remained absolute.
The realization that the image moved independently of any physical cause tightened a knot of terror in his chest.
On the third night the darkness seemed to thicken, a viscous blanket that muffled even the faint ticking of the hallway clock.
The shadow had taken another step, now inching toward the bed where Leo lay, its outline growing sharper with each breath he drew.
Determined to end the nightmare, he grasped the mirror's frame and pulled, but an unseen strength held it fast as if the house itself resisted.
His muscles strained, his heart hammered, yet the glass would not budge, its surface merging with the plaster as though it were a living part of the wall.
In desperation he draped a thick white sheet over the mirror, hoping the darkness behind it would be sealed away from his eyes.
When the fourth night arrived, Leo awoke to find the sheet crumpled on the floor, dry and untouched, as though an invisible hand had lifted it.
He stared into the glass and saw the shadow two steps further, now standing in the centre of the reflected room, its form opaque and featureless.
Its stare met his, a hollow gaze that seemed to pierce through the barrier of glass, demanding his attention with an ancient, wordless accusation.
Leo's legs felt as though they were forged from stone, each movement a laborious effort, and he could not summon the strength to flee.
He lay there, heart pounding, watching the dark figure swell with each passing second, its presence growing more oppressive than the night itself.
At dawn, Leo walked to the town's modest library, its stone facade echoing the same quiet melancholy that haunted his bedroom.
He pored over yellowed ledgers and brittle newspapers, searching for any mention of the house or its former residents.
Among the dust-covered pages he uncovered a terse report about a young man who had vanished in the very bedroom Leo now occupied.
The article whispered that the youth had spent his final days staring into a large, dark-framed mirror, his fate sealed by his own curiosity.
A chill ran down Leo's spine as he imagined the mirror's relentless pull, realizing that he might be reenacting the same doomed pattern.
On the fifth night Leo resolved to stay awake, flooding the room with bright lamps, the harsh light stabbing at the darkness like knives.
Midnight arrived, and without warning every bulb in the house sputtered out, plunging the interior into an oppressive, absolute black.
The mirror, however, emitted its own cold luminescence, revealing the shadow perched at the very edge of the glass, poised to cross.
A thin, icy whisper slipped from the surface, chanting Leo's name in a voice that seemed older than the house itself.
The syllables repeated, each echo a reminder that the barrier between worlds was thinning, and that he was no longer merely an observer.
On the sixth night, exhaustion gave way to dread as the dark figure finally arrived at the very front of the mirror, its palms pressed flat against the surface.
The glass, no longer a solid barrier, rippled like water disturbed by a gentle wind, shimmering with a sickly, blue-gray sheen.
From the wavering pane, a cold, skeletal hand emerged, its fingers elongated and trembling, reaching toward Leo with a desperate, inexorable pull.
He felt the icy contact brush his skin, a sensation that froze his blood and anchored his body as though shackled by unseen chains.
In that instant, the realization struck him that the choice to remain had sealed his fate, and the mirror claimed another soul.
When dawn broke, the house stood silent and empty, the bed vacant, the mirror still hanging, its frame glinting in the pale morning light.
Police officers combed the rooms, finding no trace of Leo or the vanished young man, only the lingering chill that clung to the walls.
The mirror, untouched, seemed to watch the investigators with an indifferent gleam, as if bored by their futile curiosity.
A few weeks later, the estate's contents were auctioned to a shop that specialized in antiquities, and the mirror was displayed among other curiosities.
A new tenant, a young woman moving into a nearby apartment, purchased the dark-framed piece, smiling at its age-worn elegance, unaware of the waiting darkness.
She hung the mirror opposite her own bed, arranging the room with care, and as she stepped back, a familiar chill brushed her neck.
In the reflected surface, a dark silhouette already waited, its featureless head turned toward her, eyes unseen yet somehow accusing.
She whispered a nervous laugh, but the mirror's cold glow answered with a silent promise that the cycle would continue.
The house beyond the street kept its secrets, and the ancient shadow prepared once more to step out of the glass and into another life.
And so the mirror waited, patient as the night, for the next curious soul to glance into its depths and awaken the darkness within.
